text_post: I'm working on a database of useful MRM statistics that only uses reliable primary sources (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets...it?usp=sharing, if you want to contribute), and I'm having trouble tracking down a source for this topic. I've seen 2 different statistics cited on the web. Unfortunately, each have their own problems:1/3 of DNA tests exonerate the accused: every place that I've found this all ultimately point back to this 1993 Newsweek article (http://www.newsweek.com/genetics-courtroom-192258), which has absolutely no citation. 1/4 of DNA tests exonerate the accused: the only place I was able to find this was in an expert's commentary on a report, which also had no data other than the statistic thrown out. Does anyone have any idea where primary sources can be found for the rate of rape accusations/convictions that turn out to be false (or unverifiable) using DNA analysis? Thanks!
